steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Odysseus's wanderings take him through a series of increasingly dangerous encounters with monsters and divine beings | Key Fact: The Lotus-Eaters offer a fruit that causes forgetfulness — they represent the temptation of abandoning the journey | Key Fact: The Cyclops Polyphemus represents uncivilised brutality — he eats men raw and ignores xenia and the gods | Key Fact: Circe transforms Odysseus's men into pigs — she represents the dangers of female seduction and enchantment
